svg.title: Selective satiety and outcome-guided choice
svg.desc: Figure 6. Three-panel schematic of Howard et al. (2020), doi:10.1016/j.cub.2019.12.007. A: Learn visual cue–food odor links; make baseline choices with the chosen odor delivered; receive cTBS or sham before a meal; eat the food associated with odor O1 to satiety; rate the actual food odors, then choose between visual cues with only odorless air delivered. C1/O1 and C2/O2 are representative examples from a larger stimulus set. B: Stimulation is applied at an accessible right lateral prefrontal site selected using functional connectivity with central/lateral orbitofrontal cortex. The dashed line denotes functional connectivity, not a direct anatomical tract. The coil and brain locations are schematic. C: Relative to the pre-meal baseline, pleasantness of the sated odor declines in both groups; the normal early reduction in choice of its cue is impaired after OFC-network cTBS. The matrix summarizes qualitative results and does not represent numerical effect sizes.
